items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.desc: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recordedMultiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains. Continue reading...

items.title: EU wants ‘closest possible relationship’ with UK after agreeing Brexit reset deal

 Making today’s reset deal contingent on a further agreement on the level of tuition fees for EU citizens is designed to neutralise the leverage London gets in the next six months, EU sources have said.
 
 
 Senior diplomats had already confirmed this week that the EU would defer the deal on the level of tuition fees for another six months, a move designed to give the UK leverage in parallel negotiations to have the UK included in Made in Europe legislation designed to protect EU supply chains against China.
 
 
 But the move to make the food and drink deal also contingent on a tuition fees deal effectively seeks to neutralise the leverage the UK gets today.
 
 
 This is a serious chess game and shows the EU, again, is willing to speak very warmly about the UK but will play absolute hard ball when it comes to conceding any points to a former member state.

Protesters across Europe are set to take to the streets on Friday in a show of cross-border solidarity, joining coordinated demonstrations against the rising cost of living, militarisation and other causes, in a bid to increase pressure on their governments. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.

items.title: French ex-PM Villepin announces presidential run
items.desc: France's former prime minister and foreign minister Dominique de Villepin, famed abroad for his excoriating 2003 denunciation of US plans for invading Iraq, said on Friday he was running for president. Villepin enters an already crowded field of candidates seeking to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, with polls pointing towards a possible run-off between frontrunner Marine Le Pen of the far-right National Rally (RN) and hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) veteran Jean-Luc Melenchon.

items.title: Shenzhen trilateral: Xi Jinping's 'masterclass in diplomatic theatre'
items.desc: Xi Jinping positioned himself as a great statesman when he met with the US president and Russia's Vladimir Putin for trilateral talks in Shenzhen this week. But while the Chinese president sparkled on the world stage, does he have anything to show for it? Seong-Hyon Lee, an associate at Harvard University Asia Center, tells us how the trilateral has come up short on deliverables.

items.title: Spain’s political crossroads, Europe’s wider stakes: Spaniards to vote in key election
items.desc: The stakes are high – not only for people in Spain, but also for Europe. On November 29, the country holds a parliamentary election that could see the end of the Socialist-led government and potentially a coalition between the right and the far right, in one of the EU’s biggest and most influential member states. It could also signal the end of Pedro Sanchez’s third term in office. Among other things, the prime minister may pay the political price for two shocking train crashes and the migrant crisis in Spain’s North African exclave of Ceuta.

items.title: Jamaica's beaches are increasingly off limits to locals
items.desc: Jamaica usually conjures up images of white sandy beaches, Rastafari culture and Bob Marley – but another reality exists. On this small Caribbean island, less than 1 percent of the coastline is freely accessible to local people. The rest has gradually been privatised, mostly for large hotel developments and private homes.

items.title: Cincinnati Zoo's famed Fiona the hippo dies days after eating a visitor’s hat
items.desc: Fiona, the hippo whose premature birth and fight for survival at the Cincinnati Zoo turned her into a global sensation nearly a decade ago, died Thursday from complications after swallowing a knit hat that was accidentally flung into her enclosure. She was 9 years old. “It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo said in a statement.

items.title: REPLAY: Burnham, Von der Leyen hail 'turning point' in EU
items.desc: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham hailed a "landmark" deal with the European Union on Friday, as the two sides sealed pacts on food exports, emissions-trading schemes and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen welcomed a "turning point" in ties with Britain following Brexit. Watch our replay.

items.title: COP31 wrapping up in Turkey: Climate deal elusive as fossil fuels go unmentioned
items.desc: The UN's COP31 climate talks were set to spill into overtime Friday as countries remained deadlocked over a draft deal that makes no mention of fossil fuels, with a host of other disputes also snarling negotiations. The talks come with a series of stark reminders of the urgency of climate action, from heatwaves in Europe and devastating floods in Nepal, while a record-breaking El Nino supercharges temperatures. FRANCE 24's Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.

items.title: Burnham hails 'landmark' EU-UK deal as 'good day' for Britain, Europe
items.desc: Britain and the European Union agreed deals on trade, carbon emissions and youth movement on Friday, and pledged to rebuild ties with an “ambitious and dynamic” post-Brexit relationship. In a joint statement after a summit in Brussels, the UK and EU confirmed agreements that will scrap checks on the trade in plant and animal products, link their emissions trading schemes and let 100,000 young adults from each side live and work in the other's countries for up to three years. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

items.title: Russia pummels Ukraine with massive strikes, missile hits Poland
items.desc: Moscow pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least six people were killed in the capital, and neighbouring Poland reporting two Russian missiles likely landed in the south-east corner of the NATO country, accusing Moscow of a "provocation." Hours earlier, Russia's Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" response to Kyiv's strikes on Moscow's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with China's Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

items.title: 'GTA VI': When the biggest-ever entertainment release becomes the biggest headline
items.desc: This week FRANCE 24's media show "Scoop" looks at how the press covered the release of "Grand Theft Auto VI". Pre-orders and first-day sales totalled more than $2.3 billion. What does the game and the franchise's success mean for the future of entertainment? Our guest is Margaret Wallace, a video game developer and an associate professor of the practice of media innovation at Boston University.

items.title: France probes suspected leak of confidential information to Le Pen's party
items.desc: French authorities are investigating whether a former senior official at the Interior Ministry leaked confidential information about judicial investigations into far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally, adding to the party's legal woes ahead of a presidential election next year in which Le Pen is the current frontrunner.

items.title: A decade after Brexit, do Britons regret leaving the EU?
items.desc: Britain and the European Union went through a bitter divorce, then slowly began trying to rebuild their relationship. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham met the EU's top officials in Brussels on Friday for a summit he has described as a step towards undoing a decade of damage caused by the 2016 vote to leave the bloc. But how do the British public feel about closer ties with the EU – and, potentially, rejoining it?

items.title: Does staggered consent actually protect young people?
items.desc: Following recent scandals involving two iconic British comedians, the UK government is considering the introduction of staggered age consent. Annette Young talks to Katherine Allen from the Institute of Social Justice and Crime in the UK about whether such laws work. Also the social costs of femicide; how do loved ones cope with such a loss, and what support is available to families in the wake of such a tragedy? Plus we meet the women who are challenging the traditions of Mexican mariachi music, a world that remains largely male dominated.

items.title: El Salvador: Nayib Bukele, self-proclaimed “coolest dictator on earth”, is seeking a third term
items.desc: 🇸🇻 El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele, who calls himself the “coolest dictator on earth”, is seeking a third term after changing the Constitution to scrap presidential term limits. His war on gangs has made him hugely popular, but also sparked serious human rights concerns.

items.title: 联合国：全球电子政务持续推进  但数字鸿沟依然存在
items.desc: 联合国经济和社会事务部周四发布的《2026年联合国电子政务调查报告》指出，全球数字政府发展持续推进，但网络连接、技能和机构能力方面的差距仍在限制数字化带来的效益。随着人工智能重塑公共行政，各国在电子政务发展方面的不平衡依然明显。

items.title: 国际法院认定缅甸对罗兴亚人实施种族灭绝

items.title: 粮农组织：全球粮食供应总体充裕 但市场风险和粮食安全挑战加剧
items.desc: 联合国粮食及农业组织周四发布最新一期《粮食展望》报告指出，全球农产品供应总体充裕，特别是小麦和粗粮，但大米、食糖和植物油的供需平衡趋于紧张。天气变化、物流中断和政策不确定性正增加全球粮食市场风险。同日，粮农组织总干事屈冬玉呼吁加强国际合作，将粮食安全纳入预防和解决冲突的外交努力。

items.title: 货币基金组织总裁：人工智能将成为影响全球竞争力和经济增长的重要因素
items.desc: 国际货币基金组织总裁格奥尔基耶娃周四在中国深圳举行的2026年亚太经合组织经济领导人会议上表示，人工智能正在对全球经济增长产生实质性影响，将成为影响中期竞争力、生产率和经济增长的重要因素。她同时指出，全球通胀上升、公共债务增加以及结构性改革滞后等问题仍对经济前景构成挑战，各国需要加快采取政策行动。

items.title: 联合国人口基金警告：世界正面临辜负下一代的风险
